title: Auditing Failure Attribution: Label Predictability and Judge Behavior
abstract: arXiv:2610.17747v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Failure-attribution benchmarks ask an LLM judge which step or agent caused a failure. A high score should mean the judge checked the faulty step against the run (a cross-step check). However, spurious signals (surface cues) that predict the annotation can produce a high score. In this paper, we propose four tests to separate checking from cue use. Input restriction asks whether partial input predicts the annotation. Cue following checks whether moved cues change answers. Residual accuracy scores judges where cue-only predictors fail. Aggregation asks whether the failure mix or metric changes rankings. Real observations motivate these tests: on three benchmarks, simple predictors match or beat GPT-4.1. In two Who&When Pro systems, a classifier reading one step's reasoning finds 95-100% of faulty steps, motivating input restriction. In one of them, error injection leaves no reasoning after the faulty step; judges fine-tuned on its labels

translated_title: 审计失败归因：标签可预测性与评判者行为
translated_abstract: 摘要：失败归因基准要求一个 LLM 评判者判断哪一步或哪个智能体导致了失败。高分数应当意味着评判者对照运行轨迹检查了出错的步骤（即跨步骤检查）。然而，能够预测标注结果的虚假信号（表面线索）也可能产生高分。本文提出四项测试来区分“真正的检查”与“利用线索”：输入限制测试部分输入能否预测标注结果；线索跟随测试移动线索是否会改变评判者的答案；残差准确率在仅凭线索的预测器失效之处为评判者评分；聚合测试失败样本构成或评价指标的变化是否会改变排名。真实观察结果推动了这些测试的提出：在三个基准上，简单的预测器即可匹配甚至超越 GPT-4.1。在两个 Who&When Pro 系统中，一个仅读取单步推理的分类器就能找到 95-100% 的出错步骤，这印证了输入限制测试的必要性。在其中一个系统中，错误注入使得出错步骤之后不再有推理内容；在其标签上微调的评判者……
tldr: 本文提出四项审计测试（输入限制、线索跟随、残差准确率、聚合）来区分 LLM 失败归因评判者是真正进行跨步骤检查还是仅依赖表面线索，并发现简单预测器即可匹配甚至超越 GPT-4.1，揭示了现有失败归因基准容易被虚假信号利用的问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes four audit tests (input restriction, cue following, residual accuracy, and aggregation) to distinguish whether LLM failure-attribution judges truly perform cross-step checking or merely exploit surface cues, finding that simple predictors can match or beat GPT-4.1 and exposing how existing failure-attribution benchmarks are vulnerable to spurious signals.
